english.title: Fail to comply with record-keeping requirements
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) supplied a regulated poison, namely **..(SPECIFY POISON..), to a member of the general public without complying with the record-keeping requirements stipulated in section 3B(4) of the Poisons Act 1972, before delivering the poison in that **(..SPECIFY NON-COMPLIANCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3B(3) and 8(3) of the Poisons Act 1972.

english.notes:
(i) The record-keeping requirements are:

(a) the person must make an entry (or cause an entry to be made) in a record to be kept by the person for the purposes of this subsection stating -

- the date of the supply,
- the name and address of the member of the general public.
- the name and quantity of the regulated poison supplied, and - the purposes for which it is stated by the member of the general public to be required, and
(b) the person must ensure that the member of the general public signs the entry.

(ii) Section 2(5) gives the meaning of regulated poison.
(iii) A person does not commit an offence under subsection (3) if the requirements of that subsection do not apply to the person's case by virtue of regulations made under section 9B.
(iv) See section section 7A which gives the defence of proof of lack of knowledge.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale.Time limit for prosecutions:
Proceedings may be commenced at any time -
(a) within the period of 12 months next after the date of commission of the offence, or
(b) in the case of proceedings instituted by, or by the direction of, the Secretary of State, within the later to end of -
(i) that 12-month period, and (ii) the period of 3 months next after the date on which evidence sufficient in the Secretary of State's opinion to justify a prosecution for the offence comes to the Secretary of State's knowledge
